brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — Introduction to CTFS - For TechIQ Attendees

questions.question: How many modules make up the CTFS platform?
choices: Three modules
Four modules
Five modules
Six modules
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—GrantPlan, Contracting, Forecasting, Site Payments, and Analytics make up the complete CTFS suite.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course covers five distinct modules that work together to create the unified financial backbone. Review slide 10 for the full breakdown of what each module does.

questions.question: What is the primary pain point that Gilbert, the Clinical Operations Director, is trying to solve?
choices: Ensuring audit trails and compliance documentation
Modernizing infrastructure without breaking compliance
Delayed site activation and frustrated payment cycles
Aligning AI investments with existing systems
questions.feedback_correct: Gilbert's world is trial execution, and his frustration centers on manual financial drag that slows site activation and payment cycles.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Each persona has a distinct pain point. Gilbert is focused on operational execution speed, not compliance or infrastructure. Review slide 5 to see how each persona's concerns differ.

questions.question: What single figure is used to illustrate the daily cost of fragmented clinical trial financial management?
choices: $15 million per day
$55,000 per day
$3 million per year
$200 million annually
questions.feedback_correct: The $55,000 per day figure comes from Applied Clinical Trials and is a powerful way to make the cost of doing nothing concrete in any conversation.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While the course mentions several numbers, this specific daily cost figure for late-stage trials is what anchors the problem statement. Check slide 9 for the exact framing.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how CTFS Contracting differs from a standalone contract management tool?
choices: It uses basic OCR scanning instead of AI models
It only handles contract authoring but not amendments
Signed contracts automatically inform payment milestones and budget alignment in other modules
It is designed exclusively for small-volume trial sponsors
questions.feedback_correct: That's the critical distinction—CTFS Contracting is the upstream trigger that eliminates manual data re-entry by connecting directly to Site Payments and GrantPlan.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The value of CTFS Contracting is not in the contract tool itself, but in how it integrates with the rest of the platform. When a CTA is signed, it automatically updates downstream modules without re-keying. Review slide 18.

questions.question: What is the word limit for the short version of the CTFS pitch meant for hallway conversations?
choices: Under 25 words
Under 35 words
Under 75 words
Under 150 words
questions.feedback_correct: The short pitch is designed for quick, mobile conversations where you have only 30 seconds to make one clear point.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Pitch length varies by context. Under 35 words is the hallway version, while longer versions work for different settings. See slide 13 for the three versions and their contexts.

questions.question: When handling the objection "we already have a system," what is the recommended first step?
choices: List all the features that your system has that theirs doesn't
Ask what their current system does not unify and quantify the cost of that gap
Immediately offer a competitive price discount
Suggest they schedule a full product demo before making any decisions
questions.feedback_correct: This approach opens a real conversation by focusing on unmet needs rather than defending your solution—and it almost always reveals meaningful integration gaps.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course specifically advises against leading with feature comparison, which puts you on the other system's terms. The gap question is designed to uncover real operational friction. Review slide 23.

questions.question: What should you do immediately after each meaningful conversation at TechIQ to preserve key information?
choices: Wait until the end of the day to record all conversations at once
Send a follow-up email before you forget the details
Take a 90-second voice memo or note capturing persona, pain, signals, and next steps
Add the contact to your CRM without any notes about the specific conversation
questions.feedback_correct: Capturing insights immediately—not at day's end—ensures you retain the specific details that make your follow-up personal and relevant.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Memory is unreliable after multiple conversations. Waiting until the end of the day or sending generic emails loses the specificity that makes follow-up effective. Slide 26 emphasizes capturing the interaction while it's fresh.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a signal of a qualified TechIQ lead?
choices: They've expressed pain around payment delays, contract cycle times, or site dissatisfaction
A named decision-maker is willing to continue the conversation after TechIQ
They indicated they are considering three competing vendors
They've shown openness to a demo or sandbox pilot within 30 days
questions.feedback_correct: Considering multiple vendors is normal competitive activity, not a qualification signal on its own. The qualified signals focus on pain, decision-maker access, and willingness to advance.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Review slide 25 for the four explicit qualification signals. Competition alone doesn't disqualify a lead—what matters is whether they've expressed real pain and whether there's a path to continue the conversation.

questions.question: How does the unified design of CTFS prevent operational friction compared to point solutions?
choices: Point solutions offer more customization options than CTFS
Point solutions solve one problem well but create new integration problems, while CTFS eliminates manual data handoff friction across the entire financial lifecycle
CTFS only works with sponsors who run fewer than 50 trials annually
Point solutions are always more expensive than CTFS over a five-year period
questions.feedback_correct: This is CTFS's core competitive advantage—it solves the whole financial lifecycle, not just one piece, which eliminates the reconciliation and re-entry work that point solutions require.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The competitive principle emphasized in the course is not about features or price, but about the unification story. Point solutions create data handoff friction; CTFS eliminates it by design. See slide 24.

questions.question: What is the projected annual savings figure for high-volume sponsors running 100+ trials per year using CTFS Contracting, and what does this figure primarily represent?
choices: $1 million in annual savings from reduced contract negotiation time
$3 million in annual savings from eliminated manual CTA ingestion, errors, delays, and re-entry labor
$5 million in annual savings from faster site activation alone
$15 million in annual savings from integration with all five CTFS modules
questions.feedback_correct: The $3 million figure applies specifically to high-volume sponsors and reflects the cumulative cost of manual processes that AI-driven Contracting eliminates.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The savings calculation in slide 19 is tied to a specific sponsor profile (100+ trials, 200 sites per trial) and targets the operational costs of manual CTA processing. The other figures either don't match the course content or conflate Contracting savings with broader platform benefits.
